What has the vine-wood to make it pre-eminent above other forest-wood? Nothing. Nay, the reverse. Other trees yield useful timber, but vine-wood is soft, brittle, crooked, and seldom large; not so much as a "pin" (the large wooden peg used inside houses in the East to hang household articles on, <reference osisRef="Isa.22.23-Isa.22.25">Is 22:23-25</reference>) can be made of it. Its sole excellency is that it should bear fruit; when it does not bear fruit, it is not only not better, but inferior to other trees: so if God's people lose their distinctive excellency by not bearing fruits of righteousness, they are more unprofitable than the worldly (<reference osisRef="Deut.32.32">De 32:32</reference>), for they are the vine; the sole end of their being is to bear fruit to His glory (<reference osisRef="Ps.80.8">Psa 80:8</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.80.9">9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.5.1">Is 5:1</reference>, &c.; <reference osisRef="Jer.2.21">Jr 2:21</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hos.10.1">Ho 10:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Matt.21.33">Mt 21:33</reference>). In all respects, except in their being planted by God, the Jews were inferior to other nations, as Egypt, Babylon, &c., for example, in antiquity, extent of territory, resources, military power, attainments in arts and sciences.<div eID="gen20198" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen20199" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">or than a branch--</hi>rather, in apposition with "the vine tree." Omit "or than." entries.content_plain: 4. cast into ... fire-- ( Joh 15:6 ). both the ends-- the north kingdom having been already overturned by Assyria under Tiglath-pileser; the south being pressed on by Egypt ( 2Ki 23:29-35 ). midst of it is burned-- rather, "is on flame"; namely, Jerusalem, which had now caught the flame by the attack of Nebuchadnezzar. Is it meet for any work-- "it," that is, the scorched part still remaining.
